question: What relative contents of N-5 and N-6 did the lignite char have after fast pyrolysis at 800 °C?
trap: the raw lignite's 51% / 26% or the sawdust char's 42% / 40%
rendered:
Effects of sodium on nitrogen evolution characteristics during the fast co-pyrolysis of coal and biomass, page 5 

In this study, the assignment of binding energies to speciﬁc nitrogen forms and the subsequent peak deconvolution were conducted based on established literature. The primary nitrogenous component in biomass is identiﬁed as N-A, whereas N-5 is the dominant form in coal. 

During fast pyrolysis at 800 °C, the N-A in SD completely decomposed. The resulting char-N distribution was dominated by N-5 (42%) and N-6 (40%). 

As for the LC char pyrolyzed at 800 °C, as shown in Fig. 4f, char-N consisted of N-5, N-6, and N-Q, while N-X was completely volatilized. The relative content of N-5 in LC decreased from 51% (raw samples) to 29%, whereas N-6 increased from 26% to 45%, and N-Q increased from 17% to 26%.
